reportDescription: No installation is needed. This page reads graphics details directly from your browser and keeps the results on your device.
identityDescription: These are the original names your browser reports for the graphics system it uses to draw web content. A name may include the graphics card, driver, and browser graphics layer.
privacyDescription: Your browser has not shared a detailed graphics card name. Privacy settings or browser restrictions may hide it. Other WebGL features can still be available.
softwareDescription: This name indicates that the browser is drawing graphics with software running on the main processor (CPU). It describes how graphics are being drawn, rather than identifying an installed graphics card.
unavailableDescription: The browser could not start this version of WebGL during the check. Browser settings, graphics drivers, device support, or temporary resource limits can affect the result. Try Refresh, or see the troubleshooting tips below.
limitsDescription: These numbers show the graphics limits this browser gives web pages. For example, MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE is the largest supported width or height of a single image texture, measured in pixels.
attributesDescription: These are the settings of the graphics area used for this report. For example, antialias smooths jagged edges, and alpha allows transparency.
precisionDescription: Shaders are small programs that calculate shapes and pixel colors. These values describe the number formats and numeric precision WebGL provides to those programs. They are mainly useful when a developer or support guide asks for them.
extensionsDescription: Extensions are optional extra graphics features. If a website or support guide asks about one, search for its name here to check whether this browser lists it.
aboutTitle: How to read your GPU report
aboutDescription: A GPU (graphics processing unit) helps your device draw images and 3D scenes. This tool checks the graphics system your current browser uses. Its report can help when a website's 3D view is blank, looks wrong, or runs slowly.
webGlDescription: WebGL is a browser feature that websites use to draw 2D and 3D graphics, such as maps, games, and 3D models. WebGL 1 and WebGL 2 are two versions, and some websites require WebGL 2. Available means the browser could use that version during this check. This checks feature availability; it does not measure rendering speed.
rendererHelpTitle: How to read the graphics name
rendererHelpDescription: Start with GPU renderer. When the browser shares enough detail, this name may include the graphics card's manufacturer and model. Longer names can also contain ANGLE or a driver name because the browser uses a graphics layer to draw the page. A driver is software that connects the system to graphics hardware. A device with multiple GPUs may show only the one selected for this browser, and privacy settings can shorten or hide its name.
limitsHelpDescription: An image texture is a picture a 3D page can apply to a surface. MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE gives the largest supported width or height in pixels: a value of 8192 means a texture can be up to 8192 pixels wide and 8192 pixels high. Other values describe limits such as how many image textures a page can use at once. These are browser capabilities; higher limits alone do not establish that one graphics card is faster.
usageTitle: Three steps to use this report
usageStep1: Check the GPU renderer name and the Available or Unavailable badges. Use the WebGL 1 and WebGL 2 tabs to inspect the version a website needs.
usageStep2: Open Context attributes or Shader precision if a support guide asks for those details. If you have the name of a required extension, enter it in the extension search.
usageStep3: Choose Copy report to copy all results as text, or Download JSON to save them in a file. JSON is a text format commonly used by developers and support tools. You can share the report when asking a website's support team for help.
troubleshootingTitle: What to try when WebGL is unavailable
troubleshootingDescription: Try Refresh first. You can then update and restart the browser, check its graphics acceleration setting where available, or compare the result in another browser. Availability depends on the browser, graphics driver, device, and resources available at the time of the check, so use the report as a starting point for troubleshooting.
monitoringTitle: Which hardware details are outside this report?
monitoringDescription: WebGL does not share total video memory (VRAM), GPU temperature, or current GPU usage. It also does not provide a complete list of installed graphics cards. Texture limits are measured in pixels and cannot tell you how many gigabytes of video memory a card has. The report describes the graphics capabilities exposed by this browser, not a benchmark score.
